title: Log Parsing With re and Counter
prompt: Write top_error_code(log_text) that finds all 3-digit HTTP codes using re.findall(r'\b\d{3}\b', log_text) and returns the single most common code string using Counter(...).most_common(1)[0][0].
hints: Import re and from collections import Counter.
solution:
import re
from collections import Counter

def top_error_code(log_text):
    codes = re.findall(r'\b\d{3}\b', log_text)
    return Counter(codes).most_common(1)[0][0]
explanation: re.findall extracts matching tokens and Counter.most_common(1) returns [(item, count)].

title: Raw strings for regex
prompt: Recall why regex patterns use r'...'.
solution: Prevents Python from interpreting backslashes like \d or \b as string escape sequences.
front: Why should regular expressions in Python use raw strings like `r"\d+"`?
back: So backslashes are passed literally to the regex engine instead of being interpreted as Python string escapes.
